body:
Dan's first New York City period ran **March 2010 to May 2013** — three
years, two apartments, the audio-engineering career attempt, and the
first long cohabitation of his adult life, with [[wiki/people/alexis-armel|Alexis]].
It opens off the [[wiki/timeline/periods/full-sail-2008-2010|Full Sail]]
tail — he left Florida on **28 February 2010**, not "through March" — and
closes not with a New York event but with a **departure**: the May 2013
return to Uniontown that context-core flags as the timeline's most
load-bearing correction.

Until 2026-09-02 this page said it rested on "context-core, the Facebook
record, and the Gemini-_58 reconstruction, not on primary message data,"
because no message export reaches back this far. That is no longer true.
The [[wiki/self/twitter|@danfrank archive]] holds **764 dated originals
inside this period** — 265 from the February 2010 departure to year end,
225 in 2011, 205 in 2012, 69 in January–May 2013 — written contemporaneously
by Dan, in public, with timestamps. It is the only first-party record NYC-1
has, and reading it moves three dates and closes the gap this page
declared.

> **REVISED [2026-07-18]:** an earlier version of this page framed
> "NYC Round One" as 2010–2014 and described Alexis as "met through
> webcam work." Both are corrected against the canonical context-core §4
> residence timeline. NYC-1 ended **May 2013**, not 2014 — the 2013–2015
> stretch (producer aliases, the Alexis endgame, the move to 155
> Virginia) happened in **Uniontown**, and now has its own page,
> [[wiki/timeline/periods/uniontown-return-2013-2015]]. Alexis was
> in-network from the Full Sail era (@alexisarmel, 2009–2010), not met
> later through camming; the prior "NYC-1 2010–2016" framing was an
> inference error from undated Twitter content.

## The move, dated to the day

The archive narrates the relocation in real time, and the sequence is
tight enough to date every step. It begins with a credential, not a plan:

| When (UTC) | The tweet | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|
| 2010-01-25 18:41 | "ughhhhhhhhhhh missed my 210m by 3 questions." | The Pro Tools exam is failed once, on the 25th |
| 2010-01-26 19:40 | "EAT UR HEART OUT BITCH IM PRO TOOLS CERTIFIED" | The retake passes — the certification is **26 January 2010** |
| 2010-01-26 19:51 | "Brooklyn here we come!!" | **Eleven minutes later.** The credential and the decision to move are one moment |
| 2010-02-17 13:32 | "off to Williamsburg" | The apartment hunt — a scouting trip, not the move |
| 2010-02-17 20:07 | "this is the most stressful day/decision of my life" | Same day, seven hours on |
| 2010-02-19 04:38 | "COME STAY. be moved in by march 1." | The target date, stated to a friend |
| 2010-02-20 03:15 | "moving to brooklyn in 9 days." | Counts to 1 March independently |
| 2010-02-27 19:02 | "last day in errrlando…spending it how I always imagined: hangin in a u-haul store." | The last Florida day |
| 2010-02-28 20:30 | "peace out, florida. it's been real." | **The departure** |
| 2010-03-24 18:35 | "a new work email address. big day. update your contacts: dan@ishlab.com" | First day on the ishlab address |

> **GAP CLOSED [2026-09-02]:** the gap, as this page stated it — *"the
> exact 2010 move date is unresolved (context-core's residence table
> starts Brooklyn in April 2010, while an earlier note claimed a January
> 3 move — the Florida tail through March 2010 favors the April date)."*
> Neither candidate is right. Dan left Florida on **28 February 2010**
> and was living and working in Brooklyn by the third week of March. The
> April date in context-core's residence table is a month late; the
> "January 3, 2010" date is [[wiki/self/facebook|Facebook's
> `places lived` field]], which is a value Dan typed into a form at an
> unknown later time, and it is wrong by eight weeks — on 20 February
> 2010 he was still counting down nine days to a move that had not
> happened. The tweets are contemporaneous, dated by the platform rather
> than by memory, and they agree with the one independent record that
> exists: Facebook's own **work** history starts ishlab in **March 2010**,
> which is exactly when `dan@ishlab.com` first appears.

The corroboration matters more than the correction. Facebook's work
history and the tweet record were produced years apart by different
mechanisms, and they agree on March 2010 against Facebook's own
self-entered residence field. Where a self-reported field and a
timestamped one disagree here, the timestamp has won — worth remembering
the next time a `places lived` date is the only source for something.

## The two apartments and the work

The residence timeline is **[[wiki/places/424-bedford-ave|424 Bedford Ave]] (Williamsburg, Brooklyn),
March 2010 – March 2012**, then **Manhattan Upper East Side, 90th between
3rd and Lexington, March 2012 – May 2013**. Both ends move a month
earlier than the residence table had them, and the second move is dated
by two consecutive tweets that need no interpretation:

> **2012-03-29 19:40** — "Goodbye, Brooklyn!"
> **2012-03-30 19:55** — "Hello, Manhattan."

The check-ins follow immediately and confirm the neighbourhood: Osso Buco
UES on 31 March, then New York Sports Club, Josie's West and Le Pain
Quotidien through the first ten days of April, all Manhattan, after two
years in which every check-in had been Brooklyn.

The Williamsburg years have a geography of their own, and it is precise
because Dan was posting Foursquare check-ins with street addresses
between March 2010 and January 2011 — fifteen of them, the only
address-level location data the corpus holds for any year before the
Google Timeline export begins in April 2014. They cluster in a few
blocks of south Williamsburg: the Bedford Ave deli at S. 2nd, the c-town
at South 1st and Havemeyer, the Walgreens at 210 Union Ave, the Marcy
Ave J/M/Z platform. Ako Japanese at 205 Bedford and Peter Luger on
Broadway are the neighbourhood's restaurants; DuMont Burger recurs as
the one he names before arriving ("zomg i can taste the dumont burger
already", 11 March 2010, written from a studio session in Florida three
days before the train north). Beyond Williamsburg the pins are Brooklyn
Bridge Park, Grimaldi's in DUMBO, Electric Zoo on Randall's Island
(5 September 2010, "w/ 115 others") and Hibernia on W 50th.

Professionally
this is the studio-work era — the audio-engineering attempt the Full
Sail degree pointed at, running through **ishlab** (2010–11) and
**Creative License** (2010–2012). It is the one window in Dan's life
where the recording-arts training was actually the job, and it did not
convert into a durable career: the thread simply ends with the 2013
departure, and no audio work of comparable seriousness recurs until the
much later GRIPNOTIC production reactivation.

Alexis was there for all of it — "with me the whole time we were in
nyc," per the Gemini-_58 reconstruction — working at the historic
**Bridge Cafe** (279 Water St, the oldest tavern in the city) until
**Hurricane Sandy** wiped out the Seaport in October 2012, a documented
structural shock to the household economy. A brief 2013 blip with
[[wiki/people/franki-faris|Franki]] ("I really didn't have the romantic
feelings for franki that i said i did at the time") resolved back to
Alexis, foreshadowing the switch-slot mechanics the
[[wiki/mind/synthesis/bond-switch-2015|2015 single-bond analysis]] makes
explicit.

## The two things that started here and did not stop

Two throughlines of the whole corpus originate in this window. The
**Suboxone regimen** begins at its front edge (~January 2010, with a
one-year discrepancy against legacy docs that context-core flags as
resolvable from the first strips reference) — the fifteen-year daily
chassis documented in [[wiki/health/chemical-architecture]] starts here.
And the **Twitter voice** — the weaponized irony and aesthetic
signaling that becomes the linguistic fingerprint — takes its mature
shape in these years, the same online persona that seeds the
"ihatedanfrank" identity later archived in [[wiki/self/facebook]].
Cultural markers of the era are dense in the Facebook likes record: the
chiptune-to-EDM progression (Anamanaguchi → Flying Lotus →
ODESZA/JAUZ), and the **LCD Soundsystem MSG farewell (April 2011)** as a
dated attendance anchor.

## Transition

The period closes with the **May 2013 departure to Uniontown** — the
return that the Twitter record's "2013 systemic rupture" actually marks
(the rupture was the leaving, not a New York event). Everything the old
framing filed under "later NYC" — SLOPPP and MOGZART, the Alexis
collapse, the move to 155 Virginia, the pivot to Annie — belongs to
[[wiki/timeline/periods/uniontown-return-2013-2015]].

**Gaps:** the Suboxone start year (~2010 vs 2011) is still pinned only
from memory, not from a first-strips corpus row, and the tweets do not
settle it — the archive names no medication in this window at all.

No *message* corpus survives from this period; the earliest real-text
rows in any on-disk export begin November 12, 2015. That limit is real
and unchanged. What changed on 2026-09-02 is that it is no longer the
same thing as having no primary source: 764 dated public originals cover
these three years, and the page now rests on them for the move, the two
apartments, the Williamsburg geography and the ishlab start.

Two limits on that evidence, which the archive states about itself and
this page repeats rather than quietly benefiting from. **2010 through
2012 are live-scrape reconstructions, not a complete export** — the
operator spreadsheet does not begin until 2013-08-17, so the 265/225/205
yearly counts are what has been recovered from X search, and are floors
rather than totals. And the archive is originals-only: pure reposts are
excluded by its inclusion rule, so a quiet stretch here means quiet in
things Dan wrote, not silence on the account.

**The departure is the one date the tweets do not fix.** They corroborate
it without pinning it: New York references run 8.8%, 8.9% and 10.2% of
originals across 2010, 2011 and 2012 and then fall to 0.3% in 2013, the
last tweet placing him in the city being the 18 November 2012 internship
pitch ("living in NYC"). That is the right shape for a spring 2013
departure and it is not a date. May 2013 continues to rest on
context-core, and on the July 2013 line to [[wiki/people/ej-rags]] — "i
just moved back.
